rule: Blind scoring separates direct Arin attestations from family-level Yeniseian structural parallels and reconstruction-heavy gaps. Traditional Chinese glosses remain hidden until GLOSS_REVEAL. Werner 2005 primary data overrides compressed secondary characterizations.

models.name: Old Arin / Yeniseian
models.analysis_source: VOVIN2016; refined toward Arin by BONMANN_FRIES; decomposed against WERNER2005_PRIMARY in v1.4

evidence.claim: A published whole-phrase Yeniseian reconstruction can be mapped onto all four Chinese chunks without changing language family mid-phrase.

Werner independently documents a rigid, multi-position Yeniseian verb template with actant, tense/aspect, directional/incorporative and root positions, making a multi-morpheme parse typologically real rather than ad hoc.
Independent Ket come-out paradigms use liquid material in past forms and Yugh paradigms independently show r/ir past material, supporting the family-level liquid past slot used in t-il-ek-aŋ.
Werner independently documents fixed object-actant slots and 3SG masculine a/o-type material in transitive Yeniseian paradigms, supporting the structural type of the proposed o object slot.

Both predicate-sized chunks end in an -aŋ-like sequence compatible with widespread Yeniseian third-person/plural predicative or actant morphology; this is family-level support, not an Arin-specific diagnostic.
Werner's independent Arin material contains a 3PL surface form of 'stand' ending in -taŋ, so surface compatibility with the second predicate is real.
The same peculiar Arin 'stand' paradigm uses -taŋ for 1PL too; Werner's generalized reconstruction gives 1PL -taŋ/*-toŋ and animate 3PL -aŋ/-iaŋ, so -taŋ is not a clean person-specific diagnostic.
Connecting Chinese ke to Arin kel requires non-representation or loss of the final liquid /l/.
The earlier Pumpokol-style Yeniseian solution was criticized for unattested morphemes and unmatched units; an Arin refinement must explicitly clear those gaps rather than inherit a free pass.

Werner states that only two or three secure Pumpokol B-affix verbal forms are attested and that no broad conclusions about Pumpokol verbal inflection can be drawn; detailed Pumpokol paradigmatic projections therefore carry real uncertainty.
Werner directly records Arin go as unkut/baxatum and Pumpokol go as bulün/bulun; no direct Arin or secure Pumpokol ek = go form was found, so ek remains a deeper reconstruction.

Werner's direct Arin foot is apil/pil and Arin take is menkamen, while secure Pumpokol evidence is sparse; proposed got 'foot(?)' and kt 'take' are reconstruction-heavy rather than direct Arin lexical matches.

Vovin segments the end as kt+aŋ, while the later Arin argument discusses surface <taŋ> as a 3PL ending. Until the boundary is explicitly reconciled, the surface t must not be counted independently for both root and suffix.
An Old Arin stage and Old Arin/Common Turkic contact are chronologically compatible with the early fourth-century setting, although the broader historical framework remains tentative.
Independent work supports Yeniseian-Turkic interaction in Inner Asia and makes an Arin-related contact setting geographically plausible.

After gloss reveal, Werner directly attests Arin kel = army, kelbaxal'a = I make war and keln'a keko = warrior. This is the strongest direct primary Arin lexical anchor in the couplet, though Chinese ke lacks final /l/.
After gloss reveal, the proposed Yeniseian predicate analyses reproduce the transmitted event-level interpretation.
A published Turkic reconstruction covers the entire phrase and supplies an internally Turkic morphosyntactic parse.
Final -ŋ has a plausible Turkic imperative comparison and is not by itself diagnostic for Yeniseian.
The authors explicitly note that reconstructed erkan does not conform to the Old Turkic vowel-harmony system they posit.
The boklug-gu accusative analysis requires assumptions about a pre-Old-Turkic accusative history not directly attested in the phrase.
The parse maps 支 to a zero nominative in su-Ø, leaving one written syllabic character without an audible lexical segment.
Later historical-linguistic critiques argue that the Turkic readings are difficult to reconcile with the Chinese transcription and current Turkic historical phonology.
An archaic Turkic variety is not excluded on chronology alone.
Turkic-Yeniseian contact and Turkic-speaking groups in the broader Inner Asian zone are independently plausible.
After gloss reveal, Turkic sü provides a direct army comparison.
After gloss reveal, Turkic ket- provides a direct leave/depart comparison.
After gloss reveal, the full proposed Turkic sentence tracks the transmitted event-level meaning.

models.name: Yeniseian-Turkic contact model
models.analysis_source: No published mixed-language parse of this exact phrase is treated as established here.

evidence.claim: Bidirectional early Turkic-Yeniseian lexical contact is independently supported by controlled loanword analysis.
Old Arin/Common Turkic contact in roughly the third-fourth century CE is historically defensible.
Contact does not itself demonstrate that this ten-character sentence switches language families internally.
Within-phrase family switching is penalized unless an independent boundary or borrowing diagnostic is supplied.
The broader contact geography is plausible.
The broader contact chronology is plausible.
Later witnesses show real corruption at the 劬/助/句又 locus and digital OCR can corrupt 羯/褐/羌-like labels.
The main witness family preserves a highly stable ten-character core and the label 此羯語也, so total unrecoverability is too strong as a default.
Repeated final nasal structure in predicate-sized chunks and independent Yeniseian templatic morphology are non-random evidence that the string may retain recoverable grammatical structure.
The analysis switches among unrelated language families to maximize local resemblance.
Several comparisons rely on much later forms without a demonstrated fourth-century chain.
No single-language whole-phrase morphology is recovered.

ablations.description: Blind evidence with later scholarly verdict/critique removed
Second pass after revealing transmitted Chinese glosses

guardrails: Direct branch-specific attestation must be distinguished from family-level typological plausibility and proto-language reconstruction.
A model may lead only because one dimension is carrying it; ablation stability must be reported.
Contact plausibility cannot be used as permission for arbitrary phrase-level code-switching.
Semantic matches are forbidden in BLIND_ALL and are added only in GLOSS_REVEAL.
A surface consonant cannot be double-counted as both part of a root and part of a suffix until the segmentation fork is resolved.
